note: 2026-09-23. Opened from a reader submission (row 116, the oak at the bridge). The park's big trees were catalogued by Rainer Lippert in 2021 and published on the baumkunde.de forum; four went live, the rest are here. Nothing below has a second source or an age, which is the only reason they are leads rather than trees. The 4.94m oak south-west of the lake left this file on the same day and is live as bhg_005: the reader's 'about 5 metres' falls between the two park oaks, so both are published rather than one being guessed at.

leads.name: The second cedar at the Konigsflugel
leads.species: Cedar (Cedrus sp.; see bhg_001 for the species dispute)

location.address: In front of the Konigsflugel, Schlosspark, Bad Homburg, Hessen, Germany

leads.verify_notes: The smaller of the pair planted in 1822, described by the city but never measured separately in any source we found. Published as part of bhg_001 rather than as its own entry, because the pair is one place to stand. Kept here in case a measurement turns up.

leads.name: The giant thuja
leads.verify_notes: 4.72m girth, measured 1 November 2021. No exact coordinate in the source, so the pin is the park. Species named as 'Riesen-Thuja' in the source.

leads.name: The ginkgo
leads.verify_notes: 2.74m girth. Below the bar on its own, but a ginkgo in a park of this date is usually a nineteenth-century planting and worth a second look if the park is ever deepened.

leads.name: The black pine
leads.verify_notes: 3.7m girth, measured 1 November 2021. No exact coordinate in the source.

leads.name: The Eiche am Forellenteich

location.address: Tannenwaldweg 11, Dornholzhausen, Bad Homburg, Hessen, Germany

leads.verify_notes: Naturdenkmal no. 78, an old oak with a sprawling, bizarre crown at the eastern edge of the former bathing pond, 4.30m girth. NOT the tree published as bhg_003: this one is 2.5 km west of the Schlosspark in Dornholzhausen, and the two were briefly confused while researching the reader's submission. A real candidate for a second Bad Homburg walk, and it carries an official designation the Schlosspark trees do not.

leads.name: The Schöne Eiche

location.address: Near the gate to the Altstadt, on the far side of the big meadow from the plane, Schlosspark, Bad Homburg, Hessen, Germany

leads.verify_notes:
Reader submissions rows 116, 166 and 230 (2026-09-20, 2026-09-23, 2026-09-25), one contributor whom Hidde calls a genuine tree expert and whose tips he rules are to be taken as true. A pedunculate oak of about 5m girth (second-thickest in the park, behind bhg_003's 5.39m and ahead of bhg_005's 4.94m, which matches exactly), in perfect condition with a huge undamaged and unusually vital crown, self-estimated at about 36m tall, which would be taller than anything else measured in this park. He says he also presented it on baumkunde.de years ago under the same name; a site search of the register and the baumkunde.de search tool itself (2026-09-25) found no matching entry, under this name or otherwise, in Bad Homburg. It is NOT bhg_003 (5.39m, bridge) and NOT bhg_005 (4.94m, south-west of the lake).
LOCATION NOW GIVEN: row 230 supplied 50deg13'44.49"N 8deg36'33.84"E via the app, converting to 50.229025, 8.6094, which is 95m from the plane (bhg_004) on the side toward the Altstadt, consistent with his description in row 166. Set to confirmed on that basis, matching how bhg_003/004/005 (also single-source GPS from a citizen surveyor) are treated.
STILL A LEAD, NOT PUBLISHED: check_every_tree_names_a_source() in preflight.py refuses a city-page tree with an empty verified_sources array, precisely the Nara failure mode (a tree published on one contributor's word alone with nothing else). We have no register entry, no press mention and no photograph independent of his own account, only his own repeated say-so, however detailed and consistent. Asked him (2026-09-25 reply) for the baumkunde.de link or a photo of the trunk, either of which would supply the missing source. Publish as bhg_006 the day either arrives.
